open_points.subject: AuditEntry identity across restored store histories
open_points.text: “never reused within that history” and “A store restored from a backup after a loss begins its own history from the backup's last number”
open_points.question: When the restored history reuses sequence numbers that the lost history had already used after the backup, is an AuditEntry identified only within one store history, and if so what identifies or scopes that history?
options: The sequence number identifies an entry only within an implicit current store history, with no stored history identifier
AuditEntry identity is the pair of a stored history identifier and sequence number
Sequence numbers remain unique across all histories by preserving an external high-water mark
open_points.default_guess: Treat the sequence number as identity only within the current store history, with the history scope implicit in the store.

open_points.subject: AuditEntry continuity when an older backup restores erased entries
open_points.text: “written -> erased by the owner's dated erasure” and “The restored store begins its own history from the backup: every change after it is lost, the audit entries with it”
open_points.question: If an audit entry was present in the backup and erased later in the lost history, does restoration make that same AuditEntry present again, create a restored copy with a new identity, or treat the new history as a branch in which that entry was never erased?
options: It is the same entry in a new branch where the later erasure never occurred
It is a new restored copy with a new history-scoped identity
Erased entries remain erased through separate restoration metadata
open_points.default_guess: Treat the restored history as a branch from the backup in which the later erasure never occurred, retaining the backed-up entry and its sequence number.

open_points.subject: MigrationClosure ownership and identity scope
open_points.text: “it is a fact about the instance” and “Durable, at most one per instance” conflict with “the import is closed on the store that holds its closure” and “present for the rest of the store's history”
open_points.question: Is MigrationClosure a fact of the Registry instance, of its current store, or of one store history, and within which scope is there at most one?
options: One per current store, independent of history terminology
One per Registry instance, with disaster recovery explicitly resetting that instance-level fact
open_points.default_guess: Make it a fact of one store history, with at most one closure in that history.

set_aside.unit: context: agreement of the earlier states' texts with this state
set_aside.subject: Repeat import after restoring a pre-import backup
set_aside.text: “the import may then be made again” conflicts with “The VPS one is the migration's only source; each is retired once the migration is done” and the accepted uploaded import file is “dropped when the import is accepted”
set_aside.question: After the VPS source has been retired and a restore loses the successful import and its closure, what authorized source does the repeated import read?
options: The owner must retain and re-upload the original VPS export as disaster-recovery material
The retired VPS source must remain recoverable until a checked post-import backup exists
A new export may be produced from the retired VPS data
The import cannot actually be repeated once the source and export are gone
set_aside.default_guess: Require the owner to retain and re-upload the original VPS export until a checked backup contains the completed import.
